nodes.label: INTERFACE SUBSTITUTABILITY — this investigation's demonstration of the paper'...
nodes.statement:
INTERFACE SUBSTITUTABILITY — this investigation's demonstration of the paper's central
claim. The paper (§2 / §Cellular interface) argues that "this substitutability is not only a
software convenience. It allows the interface itself to become the object of comparison:
different mechanisms may realize the same externally observable relation", and that "different
internal organizations may sometimes be represented through the same coarse-grained interface
when they preserve the interaction variables relevant to that description." Here that claim is
run: the flagship cell's INTERNAL metabolism is swapped from constraint-based dynamic-FBA (cobra
e_coli_core, O2-capped) to a lumped, cobra-free Michaelis–Menten / Monod metabolism
(`single-cell-in-a-field-mm`, `mechanism: mm`) behind the BYTE-IDENTICAL `CpmCellField` ports,
and the interface-level observables are compared head-to-head. Confirmed: over 20 ticks the two
different internal organizations realize the same coarse-grained cell↔field interface — final
biomass dFBA 0.370 vs MM 0.342 (7.5%), CPM volume 110 vs 99 px (10%), total acetate secreted
47.02 vs 47.02 (~0%), net glucose depleted 31.6 vs 33.6 units (6.2%); every interface observable
agrees within ~10%. The MM twin additionally runs with NO cobra at all — the substitutability
payoff, a mechanism that runs where the original could not. Stated honestly: the MM params
(mm_vmax 4.0, mm_km 0.5, mm_yield 0.024, mm_overflow 1.4) were TUNED to preserve the interaction
variables — the claim is "same coarse-grained relation", not identical internals, and not a
derivation of MM from the dFBA solution.

nodes.statement: Multiple real CPM cells sharing one real spatio-flux nutrient field through one N-cell coupling process (`CpmColonyField`) reproduce the paper's §Cell–cell coupling shared-resource-competition branch (no dedicated figure) as genuine spatial multicellularity: an uptake-capacity asymmetry alone (glucose_vmax 10 vs 4), with each cell running its own independent dFBA solve at its own footprint on the same depleting field, drives a decisive biomass and lattice-volume split -- asymmetric growth TOWARD competitive exclusion. nodes.label: The competition regime reaches asymmetric growth, NOT true competitive exclus...
nodes.statement: The competition regime reaches asymmetric growth, NOT true competitive exclusion, over the run measured. The loser's biomass GREW from its 1.25 seed to 64.5 (~51.6x) -- far above the viable-biomass floor -- while shrinking to an 81-px fragment against the winner's 3511 px: it is spatially DISPLACED, not driven below any viability bound. This study couples STATE (one shared field) but imposes no viability CONSTRAINT (no death, no viability bound), exactly the paper's §Cell–cell coupling distinction that "what is coupled is not only state, but constraint" -- here, only state. The winner's 3511-px endpoint is ~97.5% of the 3600-px lattice with the field nearly exhausted by t=20, so the endpoint is partly a finite-size lattice-saturation artifact; by t≈30 the winner fills the lattice and the still-viable loser is crowded off it (eviction, not starvation).

nodes.statement: Over the same coupling process, a different composite -- a localized glucose depot, a fast-diffusing acetate byproduct, and an acetate-consuming cell role -- sustains a cell that never touches glucose purely via a spatial metabolic handoff: the consumer's local glucose reads 0.0 the entire run while its biomass still climbs, entirely on diffused acetate. This is the paper's §Cell–cell coupling relational-molecule claim made concrete -- the same acetate is the secretor's metabolic waste and the consumer's sole carbon food, its meaning set by each cell's interface (microbial cross-feeding, morris2013). This closes the handoff-necessity argument the flagship left resting only on local_glucose == 0.0 + observed growth: the consumer's growth is genuinely caused by the secretor's acetate, not by anything intrinsic to the consumer or the field.

nodes.label: The cell's shed material does not vanish -- it becomes physical debris. As th...
nodes.statement:
The cell's shed material does not vanish -- it becomes physical debris. As the
domain resorbs, its vacated footprint pixels are converted into particles in a shared
map[particle] store, and that debris cloud keeps scattering (RMS spread strictly increasing)
well after the cell itself has fully dissolved, under a separate stock BrownianMovement
process. Confirmed: 68 particles shed by tick 16 (deterministic, reproduces exactly); RMS
spread ~5.3 -> ~7.6 over an 8-tick post-dissolution window in a representative run --
BrownianMovement is unseeded, so the exact magnitudes vary run-to-run, but the strict increase
is the robust, test-asserted claim.

nodes.statement: Honesty point, load-bearing for the paper's central question. The condensate study demonstrates a boundary forming -- phase separation, mass-conserved, with an emergent interface -- but NOT the condensate doing interface work: it does not selectively concentrate or exclude a second species. That selective-permeability property is exactly what would make the interface a functional, regulatable boundary rather than a transient or unregulated aggregate, which is the discriminator the paper's §Molecular compositions question (Fig 8) turns on. It is named here as the natural next step, not claimed as already shown. Likewise the sorting study demonstrates differential-adhesion demixing with a cohesion guard, not a molecular binding-affinity/selectivity term.

nodes.label: Honesty point, load-bearing not buried: the homeostatic plateau is METASTABLE...
nodes.statement: Honesty point, load-bearing not buried: the homeostatic plateau is METASTABLE, not eternal, and that is the physically-correct signature of finite closure. A closed toy system with no external material influx self-maintains over a bounded window (~2000 internal steps, vastly longer than the control's ~96-step collapse) and then eventually runs down (the ring breaks past ~2450-2650 steps even with production on). Perpetual self-maintenance from a closed box would require a genuine energy/material influx and would be the LESS physical result -- so the metastability is the honest, correct outcome, named as a finding rather than glossed as a defect. External-influx / open-system autopoiesis is the natural next step (deferred).

nodes.label: EVOLUTION holds spatially, and the DUAL control proves the directional trait ...
nodes.statement: EVOLUTION holds spatially, and the DUAL control proves the directional trait shift is CAUSED by SELECTION. Selection-ON: the population mean `vmax` shifts UP in 4/5 seeds (delta range [-0.116, +0.700], mean +0.221) -- one seed reverses, the honest multi-seed result. NO-MUTATION control (`mutate: false`, BOOLEAN): mean stays EXACTLY the founder 1.500, var 0, in every seed (0/5) -- no raw material. NO-SELECTION control (`selection: false`): the trait mutates (var > 0) but the mean drifts UNDIRECTED (2/5 up, mean -0.039). Only selection-ON shifts the mean directionally: mutation alone does not, absent variation cannot -- so selection is the cause.

Both intensify with stronger field depletion, and the colony saturates its own 60x60 footprint by roughly generation 4-6, so both halves are demonstrated within that bounded window. A larger grid or a leaner/higher-uptake field would run more generations and sharpen the radial gradient -- but at the cost of the same crowding that itself drives the heterogeneity. The constants are toy-real, not fitted; the selection signal is real but modest (mean +0.22) and stochastic (one seed reversed), which is exactly why the claim is reported as a 4/5 fraction, not a single-seed headline. External-grid / longer-run evo-devo is the natural next step.
